RENDERINGS: (1) the Emanator's / Ein Sof's / Creator's עצמות, INCLUDING the spreading sense → 'Self' (capitalised): עצמות המאציל = 'the [very] Self of the Emanator'; עצמותו = 'His Self'; העצמות המתפשט בתוך הכלים = 'the Self that spreads [forth] within the vessels'; עצם האלקות = 'the Self of divinity / of the Godhead'; עצם אחד = 'one Self'; העצם הפשוט = 'the simple Self'; האור העצמות = 'the light of the Self'; הספירות העצמיות = 'the Sefirot of the Self'; debate labels 'Self or vessels', 'the Sefirot that are Self', 'the Chesed which is the Self'. (2) a Sefirah's own עצמות/עצם → 'its own self' ('her own self' only under the pronoun rule); עצם הכתר / עצמות החכמה → 'Keter itself' / 'Chokhmah itself' or 'the very self of Chokhmah'. (3) עצמות/עצם הספירות → 'the Sefirot themselves'; עצמותם → 'their very selves'. (4) other things: עצמות השמש = 'the very self of the sun', עצם הנפש = 'the soul itself', עצם השפע = 'the effluence itself'. 'selfhood' is in reserve where an abstract noun is unavoidable. For adverbial בעצם / adjectival עצמי see עצם-מקרה ('intrinsic(ally)', 'in itself'). 'Essence' is NO LONGER used for this root — 'essence' = מהות. Transliteration gloss '[atzmut]' stands at 1:8:1 (first divine use) and 4:1:2 (the gate's defining question). CONSIDERED AND DECLINED: substance (impersonal/material; kept only for עצם as a philosophers' noun and the idiom 'in substance'), ipseity, being, existence (=מציאות), actuality (=פועל), presence (=שכינה, and it blurs the Gate-4 question), marrow (collides with מוֹחַ/מוֹחָא; and Gate 4's question and its resolution must share one noun). PRONOUNS (Avi agreed): Sefirot default 'it'; 'she/he' only where the passage casts the Sefirah in a gendered role; never by Hebrew grammatical gender. כלים = 'vessels'; כלי האומן = 'the vessels/instruments of the craftsman'. The dispute: are the Sefirot God's Self (R. David) or His vessels (Recanati)? Cordovero's synthesis: vessels within which the Self spreads. CAPITALISATION (Avi, 2026-10-07): 'Self' takes a capital ONLY where the self in question is the Emanator's / Ein Sof's own; any other self is lower-case ('its own self', 'the very self of the sun'). Title case in gate titles is fine. שֵׁם הָעֶצֶם = 'the Name of the self' in running text, lower-case: at 19:1:5 Cordovero denies that it names the Emanator's עצמות — it names the עצמות of the Sefirot (and plays on the grammarians' 'proper name'). NOT 'Godself'.

NAMES/BOOKS: הטבעיים = 'the natural philosophers' (the extramission theory of sight, 7:1:4); המפרשים = 'the commentators' (established); בעל היריעה = 'the author of the parchment' (lower-case; RULED by Avi 2026-10-07; '(Yeri'ah) [a particular chart of the Tree]' added at the first use in a chapter; a Tree-chart with glosses — Cordovero twice dismisses him; see entry ירע-יריעה); אמר המגיה = 'Says the editor:' (the ‹small› printer's note at 7:1:7; keep the ‹small› tags); ספר אור נערב = 'Sefer Or Ne'erav' (Cordovero's own); ספר אור יקר = 'Sefer Or Yakar' (established); מרע"ה = 'Moses our Teacher, peace be upon him'; רשב"י ע"ה = 'Rashbi, peace be upon him'; ר' חזקיה = 'Rabbi Chizkiyah'; ר' אלעזר = 'Rabbi Elazar'.

EDITORIAL MARKS: keep bracketed/parenthetical editorial insertions — 6:7:8 '[…מעסיס רמונים)' = '[… — from Asis Rimonim]'; 7:1:5 '(בזהר שלנו איתא לאוקמי בקיומייהו) (לא)' = '(in our Zohar the reading is le-okmei be-kiyyumaihu, "to sustain [them] in their subsistence") (lo, "not")' — the round-bracket (לא) is a variant flag on the word לא, NOT a footnote anchor (the anchors are square-bracketed and run [י]→[יא]); 7:2:5 '(אולי כוונתו לזהר בלק…)' = '(perhaps he means Zohar, Balak, fol. 189a-b; see there)'; 7:2:22 '[תקונא י"ח דל"ג.]' = '[Tikkun 18, fol. 33a]'.
NUMBERS: כ"ב = 22 channels = ב"ך 'By you [bekha = 22] shall Israel bless' (Gen 48:20); ל"ב נתיבות = 'the thirty-two paths' (= 22 letters + 10 utterances); ע"ב גשרים = 'the seventy-two bridges'; חכמה = 73; שמ"ן in atbash = בי"ט = 21 = Ehyeh; ל"ה שרים = 'thirty-five princes' (right: המיימינים לזכות = 'who incline rightward, toward merit'; left: המשמאילים לכף חובה = 'who incline leftward, toward the scale of guilt'); ע"ב כוחות / ע"ב שמות = 'seventy-two powers' / 'the seventy-two Names'; רי"ו אורות = 'the 216 lights' (72 right, 72 left, 72 middle); ג' ווי"ן ויסע ויבא ויט (Exod 14:19-21) = 'the three vavs — va-yissa, va-yavo, va-yet'; מ"ע / מצות ל"ת = 'positive commandments' / 'negative commandments'.

ירע-יריעה.notes: Two senses, kept apart (RULED by Avi, 2026-10-07). RULE: whenever a yeri'ah is described as made, drawn or authored by anyone — human or not — it is 'parchment'; otherwise 'curtain'. (a) CURTAIN — the biblical tent-cloth: the ten curtains of the Mishkan = the ten Sefirot; 'stretching out the heavens like a curtain' (Ps 104:2); as an allusion the curtain is Tiferet, the vav stretched from Binah to Malkhut. Plain 'curtain', no transliteration. (b) PARCHMENT — the large parchment sheet on which the Kabbalists drew the Tree with glosses, and the particular one Cordovero cites as היריעה. Always LOWER-CASE 'parchment' (a capital would make an ordinary man-made chart look like a divine term). At the FIRST use in each chapter add the transliteration in parentheses, '(Yeri'ah)' / '(yeri'ot)'; where it is the particular chart, also add the bracketed clarification '[a particular chart of the Tree]' at that first use, e.g. 'the author of the parchment (Yeri'ah) [a particular chart of the Tree]'; later uses in the chapter are plain 'the author of the parchment'. Possibly Ha-Yeri'ah ha-Gedolah, 'the Great Parchment' (Italy, early 14th c.; ed. Busi 2004) — identification NOT verified; do not assert it in the text. 'Sheet' and 'Scroll' are retired. Distinct from קלף, the writing material: see entry קלף-כתיבה ('parchment (kelaf)'). SITE LIST (whole book, audited 2026-10-07; 29 noun occurrences in 10 paragraphs; no paragraph mixes the senses). PARCHMENT: 6:1:4 ביריעות גדולות (charts the Kabbalists drew the Tree on); 7:2:9 and 7:2:25 בעל היריעה; 9:2:1 בפרט ביריעה. CURTAIN: 6:5:3 (14x, the ten curtains of the Mishkan, Exod 26:1); 14:4:4 כיריעות שלמה (Song 1:5, 'like the curtains of Solomon'); 14:4:5 נוטה שמים כיריעה (Ps 104:2, inside a Bahir quotation); 22:2:3 (2x, the Mishkan's ten curtains and the hangings of the court); 23:1:150 אורך היריעה האחת (Exod 26:2, 'the length of one curtain' = vav); 23:10:41 (6x, the allusion-entry: the curtain is Tiferet; Ps 104:2; Zohar Terumah 164 'stretched them like a curtain and made of them the letter vav, and this is called yeri'ah' — RULED curtain by Avi: a formed letter with a cloth verb is not authorship). NOT THE NOUN: 4:3:1 יריעהו (verb, 'will do him ill'); 24:8:6 ויריעו ('shouted', Job 38:7).

מטרוניתא.notes: Zoharic name for Malkhut / the Shekhinah as the King's consort (from Latin matrona). First occurrence in the book is 7:3:5. PROVISIONAL (question put to Avi 2026-10-07): transliterate 'the Matronita', with the gloss '(the Lady)' at first use only. | CORDOVERO'S OWN ENTRY (23:13:36): 'Matronita: Beriah — it is the Throne explained in the Gate of ABYA — and it is called Matronita because it guards the garden [play on Aramaic נטר, to guard]. And sometimes Malkhut of Atzilut is also called Matronita, which means גיברת [mistress], and Beriah is the handmaid.'
